html:
SMTO-POL-0022 — Shell execution is disabled

GUID: bc4c15e0-d2ec-4c1d-8ce9-de988343029f
Slug: shell-execution-disabled
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • Your account or this SMTO installation is set not to run shell commands (commands typed on a computer's command line). The step that needed one didn't run. Administrator rights on the computer don't change this.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to do the work with another Skill if one fits, for example Files for reading or copying files. Other Skills don't rely on shell commands, so they can still work while shell commands are off.
  2. Ask the person who manages SMTO to allow shell commands. They can change Shell access for your user account, or the shell setting for the whole installation. Only an administrator can change whether SMTO may run shell commands.
  3. Once it's allowed, send your request again as a new message. A new request is checked against the updated setting.

What success looks like

  • The command step runs and shows its output in the task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask the Agent to use sudo or administrator rights to get around this; it's an SMTO setting, not a computer permission.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The active runtime policy disables shell execution (shell_mode is 'disabled' for this user or installation), so shell.command and python.run invocations are denied before dispatch.

What this means

  • Runtime policy disallows the shell-backed execution path selected by this invocation, independently of account privilege. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Runtime policy disallows the shell-backed execution path selected by this invocation, independently of account privilege.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the invocation kind with the active allow-shell policy; check whether an enabled non-shell capability can satisfy the request.

How to fix it

  • Check the effective shell_mode: the user's configuration in the portal user editor first, then AOR_SHELL_MODE or runtime.shell_mode in the app configuration (default read_only); see execution/native_safety.py evaluate_invocation and api/runtime/engine.py. Set a non-disabled mode if shell execution is intended and start a new request, or use a non-shell capability; sudo elevation does not override this policy.
  • Use an enabled capability for the task or request an authorized policy change for a new task. Elevation does not override this policy.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The chosen operation is permitted by the intended runtime policy before dispatch.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
